name: Judas Iscariot
bio: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve apostles Jesus named and sent out with authority to heal and cast out demons, instructed to go first to Israel rather than Gentiles or Samaritans; he is identified here as the one who would later betray Jesus (Matthew 10:1-5). His betrayal is told in detail in the chapters ahead. Shortly before the Passover, Judas went to the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, then watched for an opportunity to hand him over (Matthew 26:14-16). At the Last Supper, Jesus identified Judas as his betrayer when Judas asked directly. In Gethsemane, Judas led an armed crowd to Jesus and identified him with a kiss, completing the betrayal (Matthew 26:20-25, 47-50). Seized with remorse after Jesus was condemned, Judas tried to return the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, declaring he had betrayed innocent blood; when they refused to take the money back, he threw it down in the temple and went out and hanged himself. The chief priests used the silver to buy a potter's field as a burial ground for strangers, fulfilling a prophecy Matthew attributes to Jeremiah the prophet (Matthew 27:3-10).
